minutes.headline: Cable committee reviewed six-month finances, flagged a studio leak and asbestos concern, and drafted a no-drone policy.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee heard the station manager's monthly report and six-month financial review, and began preparing the next year's budget for February. Members raised a ceiling leak and flaking floor sealant (asbestos) in the studio, and worked on a drone policy barring staff and volunteers from using or requesting drones. A personal-equipment waiver policy was left open for more research, and the meeting adjourned with the next date set.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the previous meeting (December 5th)

budget_items.what_was_said: November interest was added to the report after the fact; two deposits in November covered two months, and a later month was smaller.
The ending balance on the summary sheet was stated.
Revenue comes from Comcast in certain months and dipped slightly; members saw no strong sign of cable cutting. Revenue depends on video services, not internet or streaming.
Members discussed a state bill to take a share of streaming revenue and how it would be split among state, town and station; the split is garbled in the captions.
The top sheet gives the six-month spending mark to be used in the budget review.
The annual subscription is due for renewal in January.
A draft FY24 budget will come to the February meeting, with final approval in March ahead of the town warrant deadline.
Members questioned why the station, as an enterprise fund, pays rent while the school covers utilities and custodial; they chose not to dig further.
Indirect costs cover benefits for salaried staff, including a portion for an unfilled production technician; unused amounts return to the enterprise fund at year end.
Members raised possible paid drone filming for the 300th anniversary committee and a conflict of interest for a member.

decisions.decision: Station manager agreed to raise the studio asbestos/floor concern and the ceiling leak with the town side together with a member, without a formal motion.
Drone policy to be cleaned up and circulated; comments go only to the sender, not reply-all; opening paragraph dropped and wording made explicit that volunteers may not use or request drones.
Personal-equipment policy stays on the agenda; the station manager will contact other stations about waivers and draft a proposal.
Next meeting set for February 6th at 6 o'clock.

what_happened.line: The cable committee heard the station manager's six-month financial review and began preparing the FY24 budget, with a draft due in February.
Members raised a studio ceiling leak and flaking floor sealant (asbestos), and the station manager agreed to take both to the town side without a motion.
The committee worked on a drone policy barring staff and volunteers from using or requesting drones; it is to be cleaned up and circulated.
A personal-equipment waiver policy stayed on the agenda while the station manager contacts other stations and drafts a proposal.
No votes on policy or budget were recorded, and the next meeting was set for February 6th at 6 o'clock.

why_it_matters: The station is funded by cable franchise revenue and runs as an enterprise fund, so the FY24 budget it drafts for the town warrant depends on video-service revenue and on a possible state streaming share.
A leak and flaking floor sealant in the studio are building conditions that the town, not the station, would have to repair, and no repair was committed at this meeting.
